elements.evidence: Section (c) permits Company to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right during a committed term or while a Statement of Work remains outstanding.
elements.evidence: Section (c) applies to any outstanding Statement of Work and is not conditioned on there being no uncompleted Statement of Work.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right requires 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly requires prior written notice.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period or Services after termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor must refund any prepaid fees for Services not performed as of the termination date, which substantively provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section (c) prohibits Contractor from terminating for convenience while any Statement of Work remains uncompleted. Section (a) permits Vendor termination only when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, and no other fixed committed term appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Customer has a termination-for-convenience right before the end of a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section (c) permits Company to terminate any outstanding Statement of Work for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires only 30 days' prior notice, outside the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly provides that Customer may terminate without any termination fee, penalty, or other charge; a zero fee is below the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits either party to terminate whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, rather than tying Vendor's right expressly to the end of a term. The Agreement itself otherwise continues until terminated.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits Vendor to terminate on only fifteen (15) days' advance notice.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement: Customer can terminate an outstanding commitment for convenience on 30 days' written notice, receives prepaid fees for unperformed Services, and Vendor cannot terminate for convenience while a Statement of Work remains uncompleted. The fallback is not fully satisfied because neither the Customer nor Vendor notice periods meet its requirements, and Vendor's right is not expressly limited to a term-end event. The redline is not minimal because it also adds an unrelated material-breach termination regime, payment language, and an assignment of works in progress. It otherwise retains the original terms without a direct contradiction, but drafting quality is reduced by the substantial unrelated addition and by overlapping 15-day and 30-day Customer convenience-termination routes.
